newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela banks sale earmarks 20 pct for locals.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela banks sale earmarks 20 pct for locals.

text.p: Venezuelan state-owned banks Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado will earmark 20 percent of their shares for sale to small local investors when they are both auctioned on Dec 19, Venezuelan State Deposits Guarantee Fund Fogade said.
"Do you want to be the owner of Banco de Venezuela?" said a full page advertisement in Sunday's national press detailing the offering which allows a Venezuelan to buy up to one percent in each bank.
The remaining 80 percent of each of the banks will be sold to the highest bidder in separate auctions on Dec 19.
Base prices are due to be announced on Dec. 4. That in turn will set the price range for shares in the 20 percent offerings which are estimated will bring in some $100 million in total.
The popular share-offering aims to quell opposition to the sale and follows a similar scheme used to boost local participation in the privatization of telephone company CANTV.
Fogade announced in October that six potential bidders had qualified for the Banco de Venezuela sale and 13 for Consolidado, including Spain's Banco Santander and France's Banque Paribas.
